questions.question:
Given below are two statements

Statement-I: Tropolone is an aromatic compound and has \(8 \pi\) electrons.
Statement-II: \(\pi\) electrons of \(> C =O\) group in tropolone is involved in aromaticity.

In the light of the above statements, choose the correct answer from the options given below
options: Statement-I is true but Statement-II is false
Statement-I is false but Statement-II is true
questions.explanation: Tropolone is a seven-membered cyclic conjugated compound containing three C=C double bonds, one carbonyl group (>C=O), one −OH group. Tropolone shows aromatic character because it can exist in resonance forms involving charge separation. One important resonance form produces a tropylium-ion-like system, which is aromatic and highly stabilized. Due to resonance and delocalization, the ring behaves as an aromatic system. Hence, Statement-I is considered true. The carbonyl π bond itself is not directly included in the aromatic π-electron cloud of the ring. The aromatic stabilization mainly arises due to resonance within the seven-membered conjugated ring system. The carbonyl group helps in resonance and stabilization indirectly, but its π electrons are not directly counted as aromatic π electrons. Therefore, Statement-II is false.

Given: \(K _{ b }\left( H _2 O \right)=0.52 ~K kg mol ^{-1}\)
Molar mass of NaCl and MgCl2 is 58.5 and 95 g mol–1 respectively
questions.explanation:
The amount of solvent is calculated as, \(=100-(29.25+19)=51.75 g\)

Now, the elevation in boiling point in calculated as,
\[
\begin{aligned}
& \Delta T _{ b }=\left[\frac{2 \times 29.25 \times 1000}{58.5 \times 51.75}+\frac{3 \times 19 \times 1000}{95 \times 51.75}\right] \times 0.52 \\
& \Delta T _{ b }=16.075
\end{aligned}
\]

The boiling point of sea water is the normal boiling point of water plus the change in boiling point.
Therefore, boiling point of sea water is,
\[
\begin{aligned}
& \left( T _{ b }\right)_{\text {solution }}=100+16.07 \\
& =116.07^{\circ} C
\end{aligned}
\] ≈ 116 °C

\( \Rightarrow (n-1)p=3 q\)
